question: Which Glaswegian author released Hermit in 2025, dealing with themes of toxic masculinity and online misogyny?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chris McQueer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chris McQueer** is a prominent **Glaswegian** author and screenwriter known for his unique voice in contemporary **Scottish literature**.
 
• In **January 2025**, he released his debut full-length novel titled **Hermit**, which explores the dark and claustrophobic world of **online radicalization**.
 
• The novel focuses on the themes of **toxic masculinity** and the rise of **online misogyny**, specifically looking at the "manosphere" and incel culture through the eyes of the protagonist, **Cillian**.
 
• The story is set in **Glasgow**, providing a gritty, realistic backdrop to the character's descent into digital isolation and harmful ideologies.
 
• McQueer uses the narrative to dissect how **social media algorithms** and **internet subcultures** can distort a young man's perception of reality and relationships.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chris McQueer** first gained critical acclaim with his short story collections, **Hings** (**2017**) and **HWFG** (**2018**), which were celebrated for their use of the **Scots language** and surrealist humor.
 
• His work often highlights the **working-class experience** in **Scotland**, blending everyday situations with bizarre, often dark, twists.
 
• The novel **Hermit** was published by **4th Estate**, an imprint of **HarperCollins**, marking a significant milestone in McQueer's transition from short fiction to long-form novels.
 
• Other authors mentioned, such as **Ocean Vuong**, are known for different literary traditions; Vuong is a **Vietnamese-American** poet and novelist famous for **On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous**.
 
• **Margaret McDonald** is a fellow **Scottish** author whose debut novel, **Glasgow Boys**, was released in **2024** and also deals with **masculinity** and male friendship in **Glasgow**, though it focuses on different thematic elements than **Hermit**.
 
• **Nell Stevens** is a **British** author known for **Briefly, A Delicious Life** and **Mrs. Gaskell and Me**, whose work typically focuses on historical and biographical fiction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The release of **Hermit** in **2025** is considered a timely intervention in literature, addressing the real-world consequences of **loneliness** and the **internet**.
 
• **Chris McQueer** has also worked in **television**, adapting his short stories for **BBC Scotland**, which has helped bring his **Glaswegian** narratives to a wider audience.
 
• The term **incel** (involuntary celibate) and the concept of the **manosphere** are central to the book's investigation into modern **social isolation**.
 
• The author’s move away from purely comedic short stories toward a more serious exploration of **misogyny** and **masculinity** shows the evolution of his writing style.
